extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.publisher: Meta AI Research, Google Research, Carnegie Mellon University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We start with the FLoRes-101 dataset. FLoRes-101 contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and these sentences have been translated in 101 languages by human translators. For each sentence in the 102 languages, we collected three recordings by three different native speakers, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible. After this first recording step, each recording is evaluated by additional workers to assesses whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings are discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Direct measurement, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes-101 dataset which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated in 101 languages by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All recordings are kept as they-are, either from quiet or noisy environment, without any data augmentations. The speech sampling rate is 16kHz.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We apply NFC and then FST normalization to each sentence, lower-case, normalize and remove punctuations. We also split words into characters, and define the token as word boundaries. For each sentence, three versions are provided: the original raw transcript (SRC RAW), the preprocessed version (SRC NORM) and its character-based version (SRC CHAR).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each sentence in the 102 languages, we collected three recordings by three different native speakers. After this first recording step, each recording is evaluated by additional workers to assesses whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Invalid recordings are discarded, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset. About 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: We plan to fill these gaps in the future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated. Training a giant model from scratch on the FLEURS dataset will easily overfit.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation, Retrieval
